beats.care: Eating out with friends? Read the bill. In this case, a compulsory service charge was ruled unfair.
beats.what: Cream Centre's operator withdrew its appeal at the state consumer commission and will also drop its plea at the national commission.
beats.why: A district commission ruled the compulsory service charge an unfair trade practice and ordered it stopped.

cards.body: The restaurant also had to pay ₹25,000 compensation, sent to the Consumer Welfare Fund.
cards.caption: the refund the customer won

cards.body: The district commission ruled in 2024. The Supreme Court set aside a stay on that order in January 2025. The restaurant dropped its state appeal on October 12, 2026.
cards.title: A long road

cards.body: The whole fight, over nine years, began with a refund of less than ₹30.

opts: A service charge customers had no choice about
cards.q: What did the consumer commission object to?
cards.why: The problem was that the charge was compulsory, not that tips exist.

opts: I ask them to remove it
cards.q: Seen service charge on your bill?

hook: Can a restaurant make service charge *compulsory*?

learn.t: A consumer commission said a compulsory service charge falsely suggests a certain standard of service.

sources.name: Free Press Journal
sources.title: Mumbai: Cream Centre Withdraws Appeal Against Mandatory Service Charge Order, Agrees To Drop NCDRC Plea

tldr: Cream Centre has dropped its appeal against an order to stop charging a compulsory 5% service charge, ending a case filed in 2017.
